transcript.text: Sometimes when I open the dishwasher there's grey smelly water in the bottom even though it finished draining fine. Not every day though. Kitchen sink was replaced last month if that matters.
From what you have described, the most likely cause is dirty filter / food in the sump. Can you tell me whether debris in the filter or sump?
I checked the filter and it's clean, no debris in it. The water seems to turn up after I drain the sink full of washing-up water, if that helps.
From what you have described, the most likely cause is drain hose / waste plumbing / trap. Next: Run a hot maintenance wash with dishwasher cleaner. Let me know what you find.
I haven't run one yet. Do you think that will sort it, given the filter's clean and it drains fine at the end of the cycle? The water only seems to appear after I empty the sink.

A maintenance wash will clean smells from the tub but won't stop dirty sink water from flowing back in if the plumbing connection allows it. The fact that the grey water appears specifically after you drain a full sink suggests that when the sink empties, pressure or debris pushes back up through the shared waste pipe into your dishwasher. This is very common with new sink installations where the 'blanking plug' inside the dishwasher spigot hasn't been removed, or if the hose is looped incorrectly. 1. Locate the grey drain hose from the dishwasher and how it connects to the waste unit.
2. Look for a small plastic plug inside the connection point (spigot) that needs to be cut out or pulled out.
3. Ensure the hose has a high loop (clipped up under the counter before going down to the sink) so water can't flow back down into it. Let me know if you found a blockage there, or if the connection looks clear.

I had a look under the sink. Since the new sink went in, the hose just lies along the cupboard floor and goes straight into the waste spigot, so there's no high loop at all. I haven't checked for a plug inside the spigot yet. Should I loop it up high and clip it first?

Yes, absolutely. You need to create that high loop first. Here is why: Without the loop, gravity allows water from the sink to flow straight back down into your dishwasher every time you empty a full sink. By clipping the hose up high under the counter, you create a 'trap' that prevents dirty sink water from flowing backwards into the machine. Please do this:
1. Take the drain hose and clip it securely to the underside of your worktop or the top of the cupboard frame so it forms an arch (a high loop) before going down to the waste.
2. While you are there, look inside the white plastic spigot on the sink waste unit where the hose connects. On new installations, manufacturers often leave a small plastic 'blanking plug' in there to prevent smells during fitting. This must be removed (pulled out or cut) for water to flow freely. Once you have done both of those things, run a short wash cycle and then drain the sink full of water again to test if the grey water still appears.

I've looped the hose up high and clipped it under the worktop, then ran a wash and drained the sink full of water. No more grey water in the bottom of the dishwasher so far. I'm not sure about the plug in the spigot, as I didn't see anything obvious.
Good news, that has sorted it. If it happens again, start with the same check. Is there anything else I can help with?
